messages:
marta: quick sync — we need to finalize scope for the Rerank API change: weighted promotion + SDK ergonomics. customers asked for promoted items + deterministic fallback behavior.
kevin: can you summarize the two customer asks?
marta: sure — Acme wants a simple 'promote' list (items that must appear in top_k if present) with a weight boost, and FinCo wants stable normalized scores across truncation so spikes don't reorder results when candidates get truncated. both want clear contract guarantees.
tara: for normalization, are we talking min-max per request or z-score? z-score will be noisy for small candidate sets.
kevin: prefer per-request softmax-normalization after we apply boosts. simpler semantics: apply boosts in score space, then run softmax, then return top_k by probability. avoids negative/positive scale issues.
marta: product ask: we need an MVP for GA: (1) accept `promote: [{id, boost}]` in payload, (2) deterministic tie-breaker, (3) documented truncation semantics, (4) SDK helpers to construct promote lists.
sam: SDK helpers — do we want server-side promotion or client-side? If server, SDK just helps build payload; if client, they'd mutate candidates before sending. I vote server-side so we guarantee fairness.
kevin: server-side required. Implementation note: we should treat `boost` as additive logit. Implementation: score' = score + log(boost_factor). Then map to probs via softmax. That dovetails with our existing logit pipeline.
tara: edge case: if promoted id not in candidate list, do we fetch it or error? customers prefer no error, but returning a promoted item that wasn't scored could be misleading.
marta: decision: if `promote` id missing, include a warning in response metadata and ignore the promotion. Don't fetch external items in MVP.
sam: truncation concerns: if client requests top_k=5 but we only scored 100 candidates and we truncate inputs upstream due to token limits, we need stable behavior. Proposal: we always normalize over the full set we scored; if truncation happens earlier, include `truncation_reason` in metadata and ensure promoted items within truncation window are preserved.
kevin: technical: we already have a prefix truncation step for long-side inputs. Change: mark candidates as `eligible` before scoring; promotions set eligible=true even if below length cutoff, but only up to N forced promotions to avoid huge overhead.
marta: launch criteria (GA): docs 100% (examples for promote + normalized scoring), SDK helper in JS/python, e2e test with Acme dataset demonstrating stable top_k under truncation, perf regression <= 5% p95 token latency, and clear API error/warning codes.
tara: scoring normalization doc needs examples with small candidate sets (<10) to show when normalization amplifies noise. Add recommended `min_candidates` warning.
sam: do we want to expose normalization strategy param? e.g., `normalization: "softmax" | "none"`? Customers may want opt-out.
marta: yes expose `normalization` but default to `softmax`. Opt-out must come with disclaimers in docs.
kevin: security/perf note: promoted items cause non-uniform scoring; we should rate-limit number of promoted items per request (suggest 10) and total promoted boost budget per request. Also need throttling on fetches if we later support missing-item fetch.
infra-bot: deploy job started for branch rerank/promotion-impl — CI 3/14 checks passing. :rocket:
kevin: next steps — draft API contract PR (payload shape + possible error codes) by EOD tomorrow, SDK PRs draft by end of week. I'll stub server implementation to accept `promote` but no fetch.
marta: I'll own docs + GA checklist. Tara, can you validate normalization behavior on the FinCo eval set next week?
tara: on it. will share regen scripts.
sam: let's add integration test that asserts deterministic tie-breaker using stable sort on (score, candidate_id) after normalization.
marta: perfect. thanks all — we'll regroup after the API PR lands. :thumbsup:
